headline: Russian sabotage ops inside NATO Europe aim to disrupt Ukraine aid (Lithuania Starlink arson attempt, Romania drone shootdown)
dek: ISW: Russia is expanding 'kinetic' activity across Europe — arson, sabotage, drone incursions — aimed at disrupting Western aid to Ukraine and testing NATO resolve. Incidents: unidentified persons tried to set fire to a Starlink communications-equipment storage facility in Lithuania overnight Oct…
sources: Institute for the Study of War (assessment); Lithuanian PM Mindaugas Sinkevičius; Romanian MoD
fault_line: Is Russia running a real sabotage campaign inside NATO, or is Europe blaming Moscow for its own accidents and straining supply chains?

sections.what_happened: ISW: Russia is expanding 'kinetic' activity across Europe — arson, sabotage, drone incursions — aimed at disrupting Western aid to Ukraine and testing NATO resolve. Incidents: unidentified persons tried to set fire to a Starlink communications-equipment storage facility in Lithuania overnight Oct 17-18 (PM attributes to Russian kinetic activity); Romania shot down two unidentified drones (suspected Geran-4) near its Ukraine border over the Black Sea Oct 17, after chemical tankers WINE TRADER and YARA J were hit near Romania's Black Sea coast earlier in the week.
sections.what_verified: Romanian interceptions match the NATO-flank pattern (Poland scrambles, Bulgaria ship strike last week).
sections.what_disputed: No direct evidence linking incidents to Moscow released; 'sabotage' framing is Western/NATO-side attribution — treat as analysis, not verified fact.
sections.why_matters: Arson at a Starlink warehouse in Lithuania. Drones downed over the Black Sea. ISW calls it a Russian sabotage campaign across NATO. But the evidence is circumstantial — and 'mysterious drones' stories have a habit of collapsing. Who benefits from the fear?
sections.context: Background: ISW assessment — Russian sabotage ops inside NATO Europe aim to disrupt Ukraine aid (Lithuania Starlink arson attempt, Romania drone shootdown)

totw_analysis: Our read: Arson at a Starlink warehouse in Lithuania. Drones downed over the Black Sea. ISW calls it a Russian sabotage campaign across NATO. But the evidence is circumstantial — and 'mysterious drones' stories have a habit of collapsing. Who benefits from the fear? The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is Russia running a real sabotage campaign inside NATO, or is Europe blaming Moscow for its own accidents and straining supply chains?
